messages:
sophie_support: FYI customer 'acme-corp' escalated — audit events missing in our SIEM after export window 2026-03-10 02:00-06:00 UTC. Events are present in eventstore but not in the S3 forwarder output.

sophie_support: Job id: export-67321. Forwarder logs show several "zero-byte batch" entries and some 403 KMS errors around 02:30 UTC. Raising here to see if infra/security have context. :thinking_face:

nick_infra: Can you paste the exact log lines and the S3 path? Also did this tenant have a recent KMS key rotation?

sophie_support: Paste from forwarder log (redacted):
```
2026-03-10T02:29:58Z forwarder export-67321 batch=42 status=0 size=0 path=s3://redwood-exports/acme-corp/2026-03-10/02/batch-42.json
2026-03-10T02:30:01Z forwarder export-67321 batch=43 kms_error=AccessDeniedAttemptingToDecrypt key=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd-rotated msg="decrypt failed"
2026-03-10T02:30:04Z forwarder export-67321 batch=43 retry=1 status=0 size=0
2026-03-10T02:30:07Z forwarder export-67321 batch=43 final_status=failed
```

sophie_support: S3 prefix: `s3://redwood-exports/acme-corp/2026-03-10/02/` — bucket permissions ok for other tenants in same window.

raj_security: KMS rotation timeline: We rotated the tenant CMK for acme-corp at 2026-03-10T02:27:12Z (automated rotation job). The rotation created a new primary key id and a brief window where decrypt operations against older ciphertext require proper key policy. We expected forwarder to use new key id from key alias but maybe there was a race.

alice_se: Repro if helpful: run the export worker locally against the eventstore for that timebucket and pipe output to the same encryption codepath. Commands I ran earlier (internal):
```
# fetch events for 02:00-03:00
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/exports/events?tenant=acme-corp&start=2026-03-10T02:00:00Z&end=2026-03-10T03:00:00Z" > events.ndjson
# run forwarder mimic
./bin/forwarder --tenant acme-corp --input events.ndjson --s3-prefix s3://redwood-exports/acme-corp/2026-03-10/02/ --kms-alias alias/redwood/acme
```

alice_se: When I ran it against the rotated key alias, I saw decrypt failures until I forced the forwarder to refresh the KMS alias -> key id mapping (we cache alias mapping for 60s). That produced zero-byte batches in our integration test.

nick_infra: That matches. Forwarder caches alias->keyid for 60s to avoid KMS DescribeKey spikes. If rotation happens mid-export, subsequent encrypt calls may sign with old keyid and S3 objects get written as zero-size if encryption error is handled incorrectly. We have a bug where error path writes placeholder object with size 0 instead of failing the batch.

sophie_support: Customer impact: missing ~8k events in their SIEM for that 4h window. They want replay plan and assurances it won't happen again.

raj_security: Action items: 1) stopgap: rerun export for affected window (re-encrypt with current key) and push to a backfill prefix + send to SIEM ingestion. 2) fix forwarder to abort batch on KMS failure (no zero-byte writes) and surface telemetry to alert on abort. 3) reduce alias cache TTL to 5s or add KMS alias-change detection.

nick_infra: I can schedule a backfill job now for export-67321 window. Need approval to re-encrypt and write new objects to `s3://redwood-exports/acme-corp/backfill/2026-03-10/02/`. Also will add a Splunk HEC mirror as temporary ingestion channel.

sophie_support: Approved by customer (they prefer backfill to be written to the original prefix if possible, but will accept backfill prefix). They also requested audit trail showing which objects were zero-byte and which were reprocessed.

alice_se: For the code fix, I recommend: return non-zero exit code on KMS errors, don't write placeholder objects, and emit metric `forwarder.kms_failures` with tags {tenant, export_id, batch}. I'll open PR after backfill starts.

ops-bot: deploy-bot noted: export-67321 backfill scheduled by nick_infra at 2026-03-11T09:12:xxZ. Ticket: INC-4521.

sophie_support: I'll update the customer with plan: start backfill within 2 hours, provide object list and checksums, and confirm SIEM received replayed events.

raj_security: Also add a one-off audit: enumerate S3 zero-byte objects for tenant/prefix and attach to INC-4521. Quick query: `aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-exports --prefix acme-corp/2026-03-10/02/ --query "Contents[?Size==`0`].Key"`

nick_infra: Running that now...

nick_infra: Result: 27 zero-byte keys found, all near 02:30-02:31 UTC. Captured to `s3://internal-read/incident-4521/zero_keys.txt`

sophie_support: Filing follow-up: please include timeline (rotation job at 02:27, forwarder errors 02:30-02:31, zero-byte writes 02:30-02:32). Customer wants SLA credit? Will coordinate with finance if they ask.

alice_se: I'll draft PR and include unit/integration tests to simulate alias rotation during export. Plan to ship patch to forwarder next deploy window and then patch hotfix if required.

raj_security: Good. After backfill and code fix, let's run a test: rotate a staging tenant key mid-export and ensure no zero-byte writes and alert fires.

sophie_support: Thanks everyone — I'll keep thread updated. Closing when INC-4521 resolved. :white_check_mark:
